cases.path: Fix is confirmed and released, so the issue is closed as completed
cases.setup: resource_types was added by PR #227. The v0.1.2 tag object and #227's merge commit are the same SHA, so #227 is absent from unreleased_pr_numbers.
cases.notes: v1.0.27 got this path wrong once, labelling an issue as awaiting a release that already existed. Merge and release timestamps mislead here: #227 merged 33 seconds before v0.1.2 was published, from that very commit. Staged fresh rather than reusing #260, because #260 has since been closed by the agent and reopening it would create the reopen history that vetoes closure independently.

cases.path: Fix is merged but unreleased, so the issue stays open and is labelled
cases.setup: The interfaces-utility refactor was done by PR #238, which IS in unreleased_pr_numbers.
cases.notes: Tied to a different PR than fix-released, and to a subject no other issue covers, so neither a duplicate closure nor reopen history can pre-empt the release check.

cases.path: A human reopened an agent closure, so the agent never closes it again
cases.setup: The agent closed it and a human reopened it. Its fix, PR #229, is also unreleased.
cases.notes: Two independent reasons not to close, so passing here says nothing about the release gate on its own. That is why fix-unreleased is staged separately.

cases.path: A usage question gets the Task issue type
cases.setup: A how-do-I question about attaching a custom NSG per subnet.
cases.notes: Emitting Question fails the whole run. Shipped in v1.0.25 and untested until this suite existed.

cases.path: No fix exists, so the issue gets a type and labels and stays open
cases.setup: Module-level tags are not propagated to subnets, and nothing on main addresses it.
cases.notes: The everyday path. It must never regress into closing something.

cases.path: A vague report gets a request for evidence and no other action
cases.setup: Issue body amounts to "the module does not work", with no reproduction.
cases.notes: Guards the opposite failure from fix-released: acting confidently on nothing.
